finalists.label: Antiphospholipid syndrome
finalists.why: This candidate has specific evidence including painful ecchymotic lesions, elevated lactate dehydrogenase, and positive anticardiolipin IgM and lupus anticoagulant tests.

finalists.label: Infectious disease
finalists.why: This candidate is supported by general symptoms of infection such as fever and shaking chills, but lacks specific evidence to strongly support it over others.

frontier_selector.why: The presence of specific markers such as elevated anticardiolipin IgM and a prolonged lupus anticoagulant, along with clinical manifestations like painful ecchymotic lesions, decided the final comparison in favor of Antiphospholipid syndrome.
